title: Review: Water; Elements, monomers and condensation/hydrolysis; Monosaccharides and disaccharides; Polysaccharides; Lipids: triglycerides; Phospholipids, steroids and other lipids
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM04#t2 term and clue written for the game; BM03#t1 term and clue written for the game; BM06#t3 term and clue written for the game; BM02#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM01b#N.4a, BM02#N.10a, BM03#N.7a, BM04#N.13a, BM05#N.3, BM06#N.4, BM01b#N.15a, BM02#N.8a, BM03#N.9, BM04#N.8, BM05#N.14, BM06#N.9b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Glycogen
items.clue: The energy store found in animals and fungi

items.label: Monosaccharide
items.clue: A single sugar unit: the building block of carbohydrates

items.label: Hydrophobic
items.clue: Describes the non-polar tails, which are excluded from water

items.label: Condensation
items.clue: Joining reaction that releases one water molecule for each bond formed

questions.stem: Transpiration puts the column of water in a xylem vessel under tension. Why does the column not break as it is pulled upwards?

options.text: Root pressure pushes the column upwards from below.
Capillary action lifts the water inside the narrow vessel.
Hydrogen bonds hold the molecules to each other.
Hydrogen bonds within each molecule resist the pull.

questions.explanation: Cohesion due to hydrogen bonding keeps the molecules attached to one another, so the tension created by evaporation in the leaves is passed down the whole column without it separating.

questions.stem: A polypeptide made of 100 amino acids is completely hydrolysed into free amino acids. How many water molecules are used in the process?

options.text: 99 water molecules
100 water molecules
1 water molecule
0 water molecules

questions.explanation: 100 amino acids are joined by 99 peptide bonds. Each hydrolysis breaks one bond and uses one water molecule, split to supply the –H and –OH.

questions.stem: The enzyme maltase, in the small intestine, acts on maltose. Which statement describes the reaction?

options.text: Condensation: a glycosidic bond forms and a water molecule is released.
Hydrolysis: a hydrogen bond between two glucose molecules is broken.
Hydrolysis: a glycosidic bond is broken, using water, giving two glucose.
Hydrolysis: a glycosidic bond is broken, releasing water, giving two glucose.

questions.explanation: Maltose is glucose + glucose. One water is split; –H and –OH go to the two products.

questions.stem: Humans make amylase, which hydrolyses the 1,4-glycosidic bonds between α-glucose units in starch. Humans make no enzyme that hydrolyses cellulose, which also has 1,4-glycosidic bonds between glucose units. Which explanation is best?

options.text: Cellulose's glycosidic bonds are much stronger than those in starch, so amylase cannot break them.
Cellulose chains are coiled and branched, so amylase cannot reach the bonds.
Cellulose is non-polar, so it cannot dissolve and enzymes cannot act on it.
Its β-glucose units alternate in orientation, so its bonds have a different shape.

questions.explanation: Amylase only fits bonds between α-glucose units. In cellulose, alternate β-glucose units are flipped, so the bond looks different to an enzyme. Cows rely on gut microbes that make cellulase.

questions.stem: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acid molecules react by condensation to form one triglyceride. How much water is produced?

options.text: One water molecule is released
Three water molecules are released
Four water molecules are released
No water is released; water is used up

questions.explanation: Each –OH of glycerol reacts with the carboxyl group of one fatty acid in a separate condensation, forming an ester bond and releasing one water: three in total.

questions.stem: Which components are linked together by condensation reactions to form one phospholipid molecule?

options.text: One glycerol, two fatty acids and one phosphate group
One glycerol, three fatty acids and one phosphate group
Three glycerol molecules, one fatty acid and one phosphate group
Many fatty acid monomers joined in a chain, plus one phosphate group

questions.explanation: Glycerol has three hydroxyl groups. In a phospholipid two of them are linked by condensation to fatty acids and the third to a phosphate group, giving two hydrophobic tails and a hydrophilic head.

questions.stem: In a transpiring tree, an air bubble forms in one xylem vessel and fills a short length of it. Water in that vessel stops rising, although neighbouring vessels keep working. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Root pressure from the roots can no longer push the water up past the bubble.
The gas breaks the hydrogen-bonded column, so the pull is not passed on.
Water above the bubble can no longer adhere to the lignified vessel wall.
The bubble blocks the supply of ATP that the vessel uses to move water upwards.

questions.explanation: Tension from the leaves travels down the vessel only through a continuous, cohesive column. A gas gap breaks it, so the water below is no longer pulled.

questions.stem: Two monosaccharides are joined by a condensation reaction to form a disaccharide. What happens in this reaction?

options.text: A molecule of water is taken in and split to supply the atoms that join the monomers
A covalent bond forms between the monomers and a molecule of water is released
A hydrogen bond forms between the two monomers, holding them together as a disaccharide
Water dissolves the two monomers so that they meet, but no water is formed or used

questions.explanation: An –OH from one monomer and an –H from the other combine to form water, leaving a covalent (glycosidic) bond between the monomers.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly links a property of glucose to the way it is used in organisms?

options.text: Glucose breaks down readily on its own, which is why it is used as a respiratory substrate
Glucose is chemically stable, so it is transported in blood plasma without breaking down
Glucose dissolves in water because its molecules are small, so it is easily transported
Glucose is highly soluble, so cells store large quantities of it dissolved in their cytoplasm

questions.explanation: Glucose's bonds break only when enzymes act on it in respiration. This stability, with its solubility, lets it be carried in blood to the cells that oxidise it.

questions.stem: Cellulose gives plant cell walls high tensile strength. Which feature of cellulose is responsible for this?

options.text: Straight chains lie side by side in bundles, cross-linked by many hydrogen bonds
The glycosidic bonds within cellulose are very much stronger than those within starch
The chains coil into tight helices that stretch and recoil like a spring
Beta-glucose is a larger monomer than alpha-glucose, giving thicker chains

questions.explanation: Straight, unbranched chains of β-glucose pack side by side in bundles linked by very many hydrogen bonds. Each is weak; together they resist stretching.

questions.stem: To make a spread, manufacturers react a liquid vegetable oil with hydrogen, using a catalyst. Some C=C double bonds in its fatty acid chains become C–C single bonds. How does the oil change?

options.text: It becomes more liquid, as double bonds stiffen chains and hold molecules together.
It becomes more unsaturated, as it now carries more hydrogen atoms.
It becomes more solid, as straighter chains pack more closely together.
It becomes more solid, as the extra bonds need more heat to break when it melts.

questions.explanation: Fewer kinks, closer packing, stronger attractions between molecules: a higher melting point. A liquid oil becomes a soft solid, like butter in the hook.

questions.stem: A drug removes most of the cholesterol from the plasma membranes of cultured animal cells but does not otherwise damage the cells. Which prediction about the treated cells is most likely correct?

options.text: They would work better, as cholesterol is harmful to the cells.
They would run short of fuel, as cholesterol is stored for energy.
Their membranes would be less stable, as cholesterol supports their structure.
Their membranes would be unchanged, as the phospholipids are bonded together.

questions.explanation: Cholesterol provides essential structural stability to animal cell membranes. With most of it removed, the membranes would be less stable, more easily damaged and more likely to leak.
